name: reverse_brayton_intercooling
title: Reverse Brayton air refrigeration cycle with intercooling (exercise 3)
summary: Teaching exercise of an open reverse Brayton air cycle that cools air from 25 °C to 15 °C. Two compression stages, each followed by cooling back to the inlet temperature; the expander drives the second compressor. The result is the COP.

origin.course: ULiège, thermodynamique appliquée, MECA0002, THD10 repetition 9, exercise 3 (2010/2017)

verification.summary: Against the stored solution of THD10_R9_E3.EES with compare_solution.py --ees-units: 45 common variables, 21 differ (rtol=0.001); only in EES: 4; only in CoolSolve: 1. COP is 1.46677 versus 1.47004. Differences above rtol are the ideal-gas Air enthalpy and entropy reference offsets and the cp(T) residual on q_ut, the works and the COP.
verification.reference: EES stored solution in THD10_R9_E3.EES (49 variables, EES X8.423), compared with compare_solution.py --ees-units
verification.notes: The maximum relative difference printed by compare_solution.py --ees-units is 3.21e-01 on s[5] (unrounded 0.320885). CoolSolve - EES enthalpy is +125843 to +125889 J/kg (about +126 kJ/kg). CoolSolve - EES entropy is -1814.89 to -1815.07 J/kg-K. q_ut, w_c2 and w_t differ by +17.597 J/kg (rel 1.75e-03) and w_c1 by +24.529 J/kg (rel 3.97e-03) because that offset changes with temperature; COP is 1.46677 versus 1.47004 (rel 2.23e-03). Pressures agree within rtol (p[4] rel 3.06e-04). Only in EES: P, p_2, h_1, h_2, absent from the equation window. Only in CoolSolve: fluid$, written as 0 in the .sol. 10 iterations with .initials, 16 without; same root. Blank or '-' unit strings (COP, efficiencies, gamma, pressure ratios) were not scaled.
